explanation.text: The drive 2AG969SY shows a concerning trend of pending sectors increasing at 1.353/day with a significant level shift, while offline uncorrectable sectors also grew slightly [F-f4b23726]. Although reallocated sectors remain stable, the calibrated family-model risk is substantially elevated compared to the fleet base rate across all time windows [F-f4b23726]. This combination of accelerating pending sector growth and high model risk indicates imminent failure potential [F-f4b23726]. Similar past drives with comparable SMART trends failed within 12 to 25 days after this window [C-c04639fc, C-37f0ba99, C-1bc99a3e, C-c88e91d5, C-6b24a63f]. Knowledge indicates that drives with rising offline uncorrectable errors are significantly more likely to fail [K-media_health-2]. Despite moderate power-on growth [F-db94ed24] and stable thermal trends [F-f369f44a], the mechanical health remains stable with zero seek errors [F-61b17f2b]. The lowest expected-cost action is monitor at 0.859 units, compared to 1.416 for schedule_replacement and 1.500 for replace_now [Decision]. Escalation is not required as the cost of immediate replacement exceeds the cost of monitoring given the current risk profile and similar drive outcomes. The recommendation remains to monitor the drive while closely tracking sector growth.

knowledge.text: Media health attributes (SMART 5, 184, 187, 197, 198) / SMART 198: Offline Uncorrectable Sector Count: The total count of uncorrectable errors when reading or writing a sector; a rise indicates defects of the disk surface and/or problems in the mechanical subsystem [1]. In the Google field study, drives were on average 39 times more likely to fail in the 60 days after their first offline uncorrectable error than similar drives without one ([3], as summarized in [1]). SMART 197 and 198 are well correlated in Backblaze data, but not every manufacturer reports both [2].

Media health attributes (SMART 5, 184, 187, 197, 198) / SMART 5: Reallocated Sectors Count: The raw value counts bad sectors that were found and remapped to spare sectors; a higher value means the drive has had to reallocate more sectors [1]. A drive with any reallocations is significantly more likely to fail in the following months [1]. Backblaze investigates a drive when the raw value is greater than zero, but a small isolated value (for example two remapped sectors) means little on its own; it matters in combination with other signals and with how fast it grows [2].

Limits of SMART-based prediction and vendor caveats / Many failures give no SMART warning: In the Google study, 56% of failed drives had no count in the four strongest SMART signals (scan errors, reallocation count, offline reallocation, probational count), and 36% failed with no SMART error at all apart from temperature ([3], as summarized in [1]). Backblaze reports that 23.3% of failed drives showed no warning in its five tracked attributes [2]. A low predicted risk is therefore not a guarantee of health.

data.note: Media health shows the strongest warning signs with increasing pending and offline uncorrectable sectors, requiring immediate analysis. Usage wear and thermal data are also trending upward and should be evaluated next, while mechanical data remains stable.
